title: Closed lowest-cohomology locus of a supplied affine finite-free complex
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], $K$ a bounded-above cochain complex of module sheaves on $X$ [def-pc-derived-category], and $a\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose $K^j=0$ for $j<a$, every term is finite free [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and $K^a\cong\mathcal O_X^{\oplus s}$ for natural numbers $s\leq r$. Then there exists a closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], such that for every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to X$, a factorization of $h$ through $i$ exists if and only if $H^a(Lh^*(QK))$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is finite locally free of rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. This concerns the supplied affine complex; it asserts no existence of a residue model or open neighbourhood.

source.place: local matrix calculation (with Tag 0EWY), before gluing

proof.text: A finite-free sheaf is a coproduct of copies of the tensor unit, hence flat by flat_coproduct and tensorClosed. Transport exactness along each supplied free frame. Apply bounded-above flat K-flatness to K. The counit of exists_derivedPullback is invertible at K; uniqueness of left adjoints identifies its tensor pullback with Modules.pullback.

For any h:T->X put P=h^*K termwise. Additivity preserves the zero incoming differential at degree a, since K^(a-1) is zero. Apply the derived homology comparison, isoHomologyπ, and the uniqueness of kernel limits to get H^a(Lh^*(QK)) isomorphic to ker(h^*d^a). This is the private proved helper lowest_pullback_iso; no new hole is needed.

Choose the supplied finite-free rank n of K^(a+1). Apply the ordinary finite-free map locus theorem to d^a:K^a->K^(a+1), with ranks s,n,r. Its closed finitely presented immersion represents the kernel-rank predicate. In both directions transport IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank across the isomorphism from the preceding step using IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.of_iso.
